subject: Agriculture
title: Natural Pesticides
description: A fast breakdown of Natural Pesticides for builders.

hook.text: Organic farms aren't chemical-free. They use naturally derived pesticides—some of which are quite toxic.

buildup.text: Copper sulfate, a common organic fungicide, is toxic to aquatic life and accumulates in soil permanently.

discovery.text: Pyrethrin—derived from chrysanthemum flowers—kills insects on contact. It's organic-approved but deadly to bees.

twist.text: The natural-vs-synthetic distinction doesn't correlate with safety. Some synthetics are safer than their natural alternatives.

climax.text: The organic movement's strength is its systems approach—not necessarily its individual chemical choices.

punchline.text: Natural doesn't mean harmless. The label is philosophy, not toxicology.

quiz.question: Why is copper sulfate's use in organic farming controversial?
options: It's toxic to aquatic life and accumulates permanently in soil
